Donna di 29 anni con perdite ematiche va: 29-year-old woman with vaginal bleeding. Biopsy of a cervical lesion: squamous cell carcinoma. Pelvic MRI for local staging (endovaginal gel; available sequences: sagittal T2, oblique axial T2 and high-resolution coronal T2, ADC map).
Referta in ordine: tumore, parametri e o: Report in order: tumor, parametria and adjacent organs, conclusion.
Il carcinoma squamoso della cervice è qu:
Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix is almost always linked to persistent high-risk HPV infection (especially 16 and 18): the WHO 2020 classification distinguishes HPV-associated tumors (the great majority) from HPV-independent ones (rare, mostly gastric-type adenocarcinomas). Screening (HPV test and Pap test) detects intraepithelial lesions, which are not visible on MRI: MRI is used when the carcinoma is invasive.
In staging, MRI measures the tumor and decides between surgery and chemoradiotherapy. The key sequence is high-resolution T2 oriented perpendicular to the cervical canal: normal cervical stroma is a hypointense ring; if the ring is intact all around the tumor, the parametria are free. Endovaginal gel distends the fornices and highlights exophytic lesions. Diffusion (low ADC) helps to recognize and measure the tumor.
FIGO 2009 (used in TCGA): IB1 ≤ 4 cm confined to the cervix. FIGO 2018: IB1 < 2 cm, IB2 2-4 cm, IB3 > 4 cm; with these measurements this lesion would be IB2. In small tumors of a young woman who wishes to have pregnancies, the distance from the internal os also matters (for trachelectomy).
Anello stromale ipointenso integro attor: Intact hypointense stromal ring around the tumor = free parametria: stage I, surgery possible.
Carcinoma squamoso della cervice, stadio: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO stage IB1 (FIGO 2009; TCGA clinical data from the TCGA-CESC collection). The patient's HPV genotype is not available in the public data.
